about: The content standard every documentation page of a Prism model meets. It adopts published standards and style guides rather than inventing rules: each rule names the authority and clause it enforces, and every bound is either quoted from that authority or measured from the site itself. scripts/content/enrich.mjs applies the rules a machine can apply (guides, terms, structured data, progressive disclosure); scripts/content/check.mjs measures every rule on the rendered pages and refuses the site when one fails.

framework.name: ISO 24495-1:2023 Plain language — Part 1: Governing principles and guidelines

principles.label: Findable
principles.text: Readers can easily find what they need.

principles.label: Understandable
principles.text: Readers can easily understand what they find.

principles.label: Usable
principles.text: Readers can easily use the information.

cooper.name: Alan Cooper, The Inmates Are Running the Asylum (1999), chapter 9: personas

iso9241.name: ISO 9241-11:2018 Usability: definitions and concepts, context of use

govuk.name: GOV.UK Service Manual, Writing for GOV.UK: sentence length

wcag131.name: WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 1.3.1 Info and Relationships

wcag244.name: WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context)

mayer.name: Richard E. Mayer, Multimedia Learning (2nd ed., Cambridge, 2009): the multimedia principle

nngdisclosure.name: Jakob Nielsen, Progressive Disclosure (Nielsen Norman Group, 2006)

flesch.name: Kincaid, Fishburne, Rogers and Chissom, Derivation of New Readability Formulas (Naval Technical Training Command, 1975)

isced.name: UNESCO International Standard Classification of Education (ISCED 2011): level 2, lower secondary

rules.title: Every page names its reader
rules.text: A page opens with a guide: one persona of the model's own stakeholders (ISO 9241-11 user groups), the question that persona brings at this journey stage, and what they leave with.
rules.measure: guide card present, persona is a stakeholder of the model

rules.title: Every page has a plain summary
rules.text: The summary under the title is written at the lower secondary reading level, so a page whose body needs more has the supplement WCAG 3.1.5 asks for.

bound.why: ISCED 2011 level 2 (lower secondary) ends at the ninth year of schooling, which WCAG 3.1.5 names as the level above which supplemental content is required.

rules.title: Sentences stay short
rules.text: No sentence of prose is longer than the GOV.UK limit. Code, commands, identifiers and data tables are not prose; each code span counts as one word.
rules.measure: words in the longest prose sentence

bound.why: Writing for GOV.UK: sentences of 25 words or fewer.

rules.title: Every page shows, not only tells
rules.text: Every page leads with a figure (a diagram, chart or illustration drawn from the model's own data) before its first section, so the reader sees the shape of the page before reading it.
rules.measure: pages with no figure before the first h2

rules.title: Every figure has a text alternative and its data
rules.text: Every figure is an image role with an accessible name, a caption, and its data in text beside it, so screen readers and machines read what the picture shows.
rules.measure: figures without role=img and a name, without figcaption, or without a data alternative

rules.title: Long blocks fold away
rules.text: No open block (table, list, code or paragraph) is taller than the compact window. A longer one sits behind a disclosure whose summary says what it holds and how much.
rules.measure: height of the tallest unfolded block at the compact window class

bound.why: The compact window class bootstrap/screens.mjs tests every page at; a block taller than it cannot be seen whole on a phone.

rules.title: Technical terms are explained where they first appear
rules.text: The first use of each glossary term on a page is marked as a defined term, with its plain definition and a link to the glossary.
rules.measure: glossary terms whose first use on a page is unmarked

rules.title: Headings tell the structure
rules.text: One h1 per page, no skipped heading levels, and headings in sentence case.
rules.measure: pages with more than one h1, a skipped level, or a title-case heading

rules.title: Links say where they go
rules.text: No link text is a bare instruction like "here", "click here", "read more" or "this".
rules.measure: links whose whole text is a word on the list

rules.title: No filler words
rules.text: Prose leaves out words the Google style guide lists as condescending or empty: simply, just, easy, easily, obviously, seamlessly, basically, of course.

rules.title: Machines read the page too
rules.text: Every page carries Schema.org TechArticle data naming its Diátaxis type, its journey stage and its reader, keeps its Markdown twin, and is listed in llms.txt.
rules.measure: pages without valid JSON-LD, twin or llms.txt entry
